content: WD repeat-containing protein 3 (WDR3) is a protein in humans encoded by the WDR3 gene. This gene produces a nuclear protein that contains 10 WD repeats. WD repeats are structural motifs approximately 30 to 40 amino acids in length, characterized by several conserved residues, typically including a tryptophan-aspartic acid (Trp-Asp) sequence at the C-terminal end. Proteins within the WD repeat family are implicated in a wide range of cellular processes, such as cell cycle progression, signal transduction, apoptosis, and gene regulation. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of WDR3. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Wdr3tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This initiative is a high-throughput mutagenesis project aimed at generating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers. Male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of WDR3 deletion. A total of 24 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and two significant abnormalities were identified. No homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, and none survived to the weaning stage. The remaining tests were performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice, and no additional significant abnormalities were observed in these animals.
